A book is primarily made of paper (pages) and a binding material (such as glue, thread, or metal rings) that holds the pages together, often enclosed in a cover made of paper, cardboard, or leather.

Regarding the text provided: "The committee has finished its work, and they have submitted its report to the board."

There is a pronoun-antecedent agreement error. The antecedent "committee" is a collective noun. In the first clause, it is treated as singular ("its work"). In the second clause, it is treated as plural ("they") and then singular again ("its report"). To maintain consistency, you should treat the collective noun as either entirely singular or entirely plural.

Here are two corrected versions:

**Option 1 (Treating the committee as a singular unit):**
The committee has finished its work, and it has submitted its report to the board.

**Option 2 (Treating the committee as individual members):**
The committee have finished their work, and they have submitted their report to the board.

(Note: In American English, collective nouns are typically treated as singular, so Option 1 is more common. In British English, treating them as plural is also acceptable.)
